notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1; none were wrong.
The Pi model is not named; raspberry-pi-4-gpio is used with physical pin numbers. From the image's pin labels: 5V = pin 2, GP4 = pin 7, GP17 = pin 11, GND = pin 39.

Breadboard naming follows the catalogue: bank 'b' is rows f-j, which holds the sensor (the image's upper half). Bank 't' is rows a-e, which holds the resistors. The ground rail is the lower rail pair, 'bn'.
Rail hole numbers (bn.12, bn.24, bn.28) are estimated from the image. All holes of a rail are one strip, so the exact numbers don't change the circuit.
The sensor sits in row j, columns 1-4 (VCC, Trig, Echo, GND). Jumper wires go in row f of the same columns.

Trig goes straight to GPIO4 (pin 7). Echo goes through the divider: wire3 to 4t.d, then the 330 ohm resistor from column 4 to column 8, then the 470 ohm resistor from column 8 to column 12, then wire6 to ground. GPIO17 (pin 11) taps column 8, the divider midpoint, about 2.9 V, which is safe for the 3.3 V input.
In the image the 330 ohm resistor is the orange-banded one and the 470 ohm resistor is the yellow-violet-banded one.
